method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. selected.text: And, for the tranquility and repose of the hearts, there is no other means save the commemoration of almighty God.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that there is no means for the repose of hearts save the commemoration of God; a foundational statement of remembrance as peace.

selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh stating that every goodly mention returns to God, the Answerer of those in distress; a concise assurance for the afflicted.

selected.text: O honored pilgrim, memorize this prayer and recite it at the threshold of the All-Merciful during times of joy and fragrance.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding a pilgrim memorize a prayer and recite it at the threshold in times of joy; a practical instruction for devotional practice.

selected.text: Supplications and entreaties were made at the Most Exalted Threshold on behalf of Mr. Strakhan and healing was sought for him
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recording supplications at the Most Exalted Threshold seeking healing for Mr. Strakhan; a named historical instance of healing prayer.

selected.text: We beseech God, exalted be He, to ordain for thee through His Most Exalted Pen that which He hath destined for His chosen ones.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh beseeching that the recipient be granted what is destined for His chosen ones; the closing linked reading kept so the guide still ends on prayer for another.

selected.text: There is no call but He heareth it, and no deed but He seeth it. Verily, He is with those who love Him and make mention of Him.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh affirming that no call goes unheard and no deed unseen, and that God is with those who make mention of Him; the guide’s basic assurance of being heard.

selected.text: On your behalf, I bow my head and hair at the Sacred Threshold and anoint them with that pure dust, and I visit the Holy Shrine.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that on the recipient’s behalf He bows His head at the Sacred Threshold and visits the Holy Shrine; an early example of prayer across distance.

selected.text: Praise be to God, the prayers and entreaties of Abdul-Baha in the Abha Kingdom were accepted and you became successful in service.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that His prayers were accepted and the recipient became successful in service; prayer bearing fruit in service.

selected.text: Can any of these circumstances be changed by prayer?  Yes, prayer might prevent the strong wind from blowing out the light of the lamp
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answering that prayer might prevent the strong wind from blowing out the lamp; a reply on what prayer can change.

selected.text: My turning toward thee cannot be equaled by the treasures of the world nor by what hath been witnessed and mentioned among the nations
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh stating that His turning toward the recipient cannot be equaled by the treasures of the world; the worth of a divine reply.

selected.text: Whoso hears the Call with true hearing, the veils of the world shall not prevent him, nor shall the mists of the nations withhold him.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh stating that whoso hears the Call with true hearing is not held back by the veils of the world; true hearing as response.

selected.text: Recite these prayers during the nights as ye are witnesses. All your desires shall be fulfilled thereby, if ye believe and are convinced.
selected.reason: Tablet of the Báb bidding the believers recite prayers in the night and promising that all desires shall be fulfilled for those who believe; an assurance preserved within its historical form.

selected.text: prayer is obligatory and required for all. You must certainly guide everyone to perform their prayers, for it is the ascension of spirits and the lamp of the hearts of the righteous. It is the living waters of the paradise of good
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá declaring obligatory prayer required of all and calling it the ascension of spirits and the lamp of the hearts of the righteous; the guide’s statement on obligatory prayer.

selected.text: Verily He answereth whosoever calleth upon Him and turneth unto whosoever hath turned unto Him. He, verily, is the Near One, the Watchful.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh declaring that God answers whoever calls upon Him and turns to whoever turns to Him, the Near One; a foundational assurance of response.

selected.text: O my Lord! Thou seest that he hath turned toward Thee and appeared before Thy face, and the might of the wicked ones hath not deterred him
selected.reason: Prayer of Bahá’u’lláh for one who has turned to God undeterred by the might of the wicked; courage in turning to God.

selected.text: We heard his call and answered him that the rapture of the Call might seize him and draw him with his heart near unto My luminous horizon.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh stating that a call was answered so that the rapture of the Call might draw the heart near; the purpose of the reply.

selected.text: We beseech God to assist them with the hosts of the seen and the unseen, and to aid them to champion His Cause, the Mighty, the Wondrous.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh beseeching God to assist the friends with the hosts of the seen and the unseen to champion His Cause; a prayer that keeps the absent friends in remembrance.

selected.text: When I reach the Shrine of Baha'u'llah, I shall lay my head on the Sacred Threshold and beseech confirmation for every one of the friends.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promising to lay His head at the Shrine of Bahá’u’lláh and beseech confirmation for every friend; a narrative of intercession across distance.

selected.text: We beseech God that through thy remembrance and supplication He may raise up servants in the earth. Verily He is the Powerful, the Mighty.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh beseeching God that through the recipient’s remembrance and supplication He may raise up servants in the earth; prayer bearing fruit in others.

selected.text: We have heard thy call and have answered thee with that which shall endure as long as the Kingdom of God, the Lord of Lords, shall endure.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh answering a call with that which shall endure as long as the Kingdom of God; the enduring reply named in the arc.

selected.text: Wert thou to gather all that hath been revealed for thee, thou wouldst find it a book wherein every word indicateth thy Lord's loving care.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh stating that all revealed for the recipient, gathered, would form a book in which every word shows God’s loving care; a memorable image of remembrance.

selected.text: He will assist you through a power that proceedeth from Him and ordain for you that which shall endure as long as His own kingdom shall endure
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh promising assistance through divine power and what will endure as long as His kingdom; a reply that endures.

selected.text: According to thy wish, I prayed and implored at the Threshold of Oneness and asked for thee this great Blessing and these Illustrious Bounties.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying that, according to the recipient’s wish, He prayed at the Threshold of Oneness for this blessing; a direct reply to a request for prayer.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding the recipient endeavor and pray that firmness and steadfastness may grow day by day; joins effort and prayer.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaching that thanksgiving for a bounty is to be raised up with divine attributes and engage in teaching; opens the test of spiritual power in deeds.

selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding His family and friends ask confirmations for particular servants whenever they pray; practical counsel on intercession.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing His supplication night and day with utmost humility at the Divine threshold; His constant intercession.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá affirming that the recipient witnessed the power of the confirmations of the Most Great Name; testimony to experienced power.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that a hundred thousand tongues each offering a hundred thousand thanks could not repay the gift received; carries the theme of gratitude named in the introduction.

selected.reference: (31 Dec. 1954 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi)
selected.text: The true basis of prayer is for the individual to hold himself as a reed, through which the Holy Spirit may flow. His will should be completely submissive to the Will of God. When this is done, then the Hosts of the Unseen Kingdom have an opportunity to assist and direct the individual. Thus it may be seen that sometimes the answer is not what is expected by the individual, but what is best for the Cause of God. importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference LG#1845 (8 Dec. 1935 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied elided extract, written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, states that the core of religious faith is the mystical feeling uniting man with God, brought about and maintained by meditation and prayer; that accepting and observing the teachings is not sufficient without cultivating spirituality, chiefly through prayer; that the Bahá’í Faith, like all Divine Religions, is fundamentally mystic in character; and that prayer is indispensable to inner spiritual development, the foundation and purpose of religion. No authority is asserted; keep on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference (27 Jan. 1945 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, "Excellence in All Things" #46) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, states that believers should set an example in their lives and conduct, that not everyone achieves victory over self easily or rapidly, that the Cause has the spiritual power to re-create us if we make the effort to let that power influence us, that the greatest help in this is prayer, and that we must both supplicate Bahá’u’lláh to overcome our failings and exert our own will-power. No authority is asserted; keep on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, given as Qur’an 29:45 with no translator named, bids the reader recite what is sent of the Book and establish regular prayer, for prayer restrains from shameful and unjust deeds, and remembrance of God is the greatest thing in life. It is a comparative text outside the Bahá’í Writings. No authority is asserted; keep on merit as a comparative perspective.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference LG#1508 (22 Aug. 1957 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, states that teaching is the source of divine confirmation, that prayer for guidance must be followed by meditation on the best methods of action and then by action itself, and that even imperfect action matters less than acting, because prayers can only be answered through action and God can use a wrong action to show the right pathway. No authority is asserted; keep on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference (31 Dec. 1954 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, describes the true basis of prayer as holding oneself as a reed through which the Holy Spirit may flow, with the will submissive to the Will of God; states that the answer is sometimes not what the individual expects but what is best for the Cause of God; and names three elements of prayer, meditation, supplication and action, stressing that a prayer can be answered only while the individual is acting. No authority is asserted; keep on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference M63-86 214.5 (pilgrim notes of Ruth Moffett) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. As pilgrim notes it carries no authority. No authority is asserted; keep on merit as a reported practical method, clearly labelled.
